editionData.title: Ebola cases in DRC hit 5,515 as Pope Leo urges global action to save lives; Iran’s parliament advances plans for charging Hormuz...
editionData.description: Global headlines: Ebola cases in DRC hit 5,515 as Pope Leo urges global action to save lives (Case fatality rate climbs to nearly 48 percent in DRC, meaning almost one in two people infected with Ebola are dying); Iran’s parliament advances plans for charging Hormuz service fees (US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says Washington aims to 'sever every economic lifeline' that sustains Iran); and US envoy Tom Barrack retracts comment that Syria’s Golan is occupied (Ambassador to Turkiye says US policy of recognising Israel's claimed sovereignty over Syrian territory is 'unchanged'). Markets leaned higher, with 4 of 7 tracked indexes up; HANG SENG INDEX down 1.92% was the largest move. Benchmarks tracked: S&P 500, NASDAQ Composite, Euronext 100 Index, and Public Joint-Stock Company Moscow Exchange MICEX-RTS plus 3 more indexes. Hacker News: Everything I own, owned (Turning Claude loose on the firmware of five USB and WiFi peripherals, and finding a command shell in a microphone, a defeatable webcam...); How I find problems to solve as a staff engineer (How listening broadly turns everyday problems into useful project ideas); and Anthropic's best AI model struggles to attract users as cheaper tools thrive (ft.com: Anthropic's best AI model struggles to attract users as cheaper tools thrive). Product Hunt features Claude Academy (The Official Learning Hub by Anthropic), Aximote (Your car data, finally in your pocket), and Yattayo (A physical slider to-do board, faithfully rebuilt in 3D).
